new_hypothesis.name: repeat_deployer_reputation
new_hypothesis.mechanism: A pump.fun creator wallet whose PRIOR token graduated carries portable distribution infrastructure (a warmed Telegram/X audience, KOL relationships, MM/CEX contacts) that re-deploys attention onto its next mint, so a token from a previously-graduated creator graduates and runs at a materially higher rate than one from a cold wallet.
new_hypothesis.persistence: The signal is known AT MINT TIME, before the first candle prints (true leading signal). Snipers optimize the TOKEN first-3-minute on-chain stats (volume, buyers, dev-buy) and almost none join the creator wallet to its launch history, so the second-order who-made-this signal stays cheap to read and unarbitraged; with <1% baseline graduation (~1 in 200 of ~30k daily mints) even one prior graduation is a multi-sigma outlier.
new_hypothesis.entry_rules: Phase-1 LOG-ONLY. For every new pump.fun mint the bot sees, record the creator wallet (frontend-api-v3 coins/{mint}.creator). Maintain a running per-creator tally: count prior mints by that creator and how many crossed the ~$69k graduation / Raydium-migration threshold (creator_prior_graduations). Flag mints whose creator has >=1 prior graduation. Log forward outcome (did this mint graduate? max return in first 6h?). After ~2-4 weeks, test whether creator_prior_graduations>=1 lifts graduation rate / forward return vs cold creators. Only then size a live entry (e.g. boost or new entry on flagged-creator mints that also pass security).
new_hypothesis.data_required: pump.fun Frontend API v3 (https://frontend-api-v3.pump.fun/coins/{mint}) exposes creator per coin (FREE, no key); per-creator coin list via same API or Bitquery free Pump.fun endpoint (creation + migration events keyed by creator). Zero SOL cost, no funded wallet.
new_hypothesis.evidence: Bubblemaps deployer-tracing documents stable creator->token on-chain identity clusters (e.g. @beaverd) proving creator-to-mint linkage is reproducible, not noise. Platform data (The Block / SolanaFloor, June 2026): pump.fun regained ~95% launchpad share after letsBONK collapse and graduation baseline sits ~1%, so a previously-graduated creator is a rare high-information event. The creator field is exposed free per-mint. No published quantified lift study found -> Phase-1 shadow-logging is exactly how to measure true lift before trusting it (honest caveat from scout).

proposals_for_survival_brain.justification: REQ-024 fix. ROOT CAUSE (code+docs+live verified): (a) the logger opens a SECOND simultaneous websocket to wss://pumpportal.fun/api/data (start_bonding_velocity_logger @degen_bot.py:4386/4545, subscribeNewToken+subscribeTokenTrade) separate from the graduation listener (start_pumpfun_grad_listener @4135, subscribeMigration), both started @15064/15070 -- violates PumpPortal "ONLY USE ONE WEBSOCKET CONNECTION" rule (blacklist risk); AND (b) the DECISIVE blocker: subscribeTokenTrade is METERED 0.01 SOL/10k events and REQUIRES an API key + linked wallet funded >=0.02 SOL. The bot keyless connection gets subscribeNewToken free but its subscribeTokenTrade is accepted-but-never-serviced -> buy_count=0 on all 2000 entries. CORRECTED ARCHITECTURE (two options): OPTION B (RECOMMENDED, FREE): drop subscribeTokenTrade entirely; keep free keyless subscribeNewToken for new-mint detection; for flagged top-velocity mints, at +5m poll Bitquery free GraphQL DEXTrades(ProtocolName:pump){count, count(distinct: Transaction_Signer, if:{buy})} to compute buy_count + distinct_buyers, and read vSolInBondingCurve velocity via periodic getAccountInfo on the bonding-curve PDA using the paid Alchemy RPC the bot already has. Zero SOL cost, no funded wallet. OPTION A (streaming, costs SOL): multiplex onto the SINGLE existing graduation connection -- the grad handler blindly persists every raw event with no txType switch, so switch on evt.txType: migrate->_persist_pumpfun_grad_event (untouched logic), create->velocity register, buy/sell->velocity _handle -- AND add a PumpPortal API key + fund the linked wallet >=0.02 SOL, capping the watched cohort to <=50 flagged mints to bound metering.

OPTION A risks small metered SOL spend (bounded by the <=50-mint cohort cap and the 0.05 SOL/wk kill) plus the one-connection-rule blacklist risk if the second socket is not removed.

request_responses.finding: ALL FOUR ASKS SERVICED. ASK 1 (two-connection drop): code audit CONFIRMED two SEPARATE simultaneous websockets to wss://pumpportal.fun/api/data -- start_pumpfun_grad_listener (degen_bot.py:4135, subscribeMigration) and start_bonding_velocity_logger (4386/inner _loop 4545, subscribeNewToken @4554 + subscribeTokenTrade @4560), both launched @15064/15070. This violates the verbatim PumpPortal rule "PLEASE ONLY USE ONE WEBSOCKET CONNECTION AT A TIME" (blacklist risk). HOWEVER a live keyless WS test could NOT prove event-suppression is the cause (low-volume confounder: fresh mints have ~0 immediate trades, so even a LONE control connection returned 0 trade events in 3 of 4 runs; only run 1 saw 2 trades, and there the 2nd connection got 0 -- directional but n too small). ASK 3 (metering) supplied the DECISIVE root cause instead. ASK 3: CONFIRMED via docs -- subscribeNewToken is "For token creation events. (Free)"; subscribeTokenTrade is "Metered at 0.01 SOL per 10000 events" AND "Subscribing to tokens or accounts requires a PumpPortal API key and linked wallet funded with at least 0.02 SOL". The bot keyless connection is accepted and streams subscribeNewToken free, but its keyless subscribeTokenTrade is accepted-but-never-serviced -> buy_count=0 on every entry. This DIRECTLY OVERTURNS run-311 "no API key / no payment path = free" claim. ASK 2 (corrected architecture): OPTION B RECOMMENDED (FREE, no funded wallet): drop subscribeTokenTrade; keep free keyless subscribeNewToken; for flagged top-velocity mints poll Bitquery free GraphQL DEXTrades(ProtocolName:pump){count, count(distinct: Transaction_Signer, if:{buy})} at +5m for buy_count+distinct_buyers, and read vSolInBondingCurve velocity via periodic getAccountInfo on the bonding-curve PDA on the already-paid Alchemy RPC. OPTION A (streaming, costs SOL): multiplex onto the SINGLE existing graduation connection by switching on evt.txType (migrate->_persist_pumpfun_grad_event untouched; create->velocity register; buy/sell->velocity _handle) AND add an API key + fund the wallet >=0.02 SOL, capping the cohort to <=50 mints. ASK 4 (buffer redesign): keep the 2000-entry raw ring as-is; add a SEPARATE append-only sol_bonding_flagged_log.json (never truncated). Write trigger: in _finalize_entry (degen_bot.py:4457) when st[flagged] is True (top-decile via _flag_top_decile @4403), append the flagged record IN ADDITION to the ring. Fields: mint, t0_iso, velocity_sol_per_min, diversity_ratio, mcap_at_flag_sol, fwd_ret_10m_pct, fwd_ret_30m_pct, graduated_bool, time_to_graduation_s, resolved_bool. Forward returns: write with nulls + resolved_bool=false and push (mint,t0) to a pending-resolution queue; the existing 15s _sweep (@4488) already computes ret10/ret30 at age 900s/2100s -> on resolution rewrite the matching record in place. Disk: ~450 B/record; N=50 ~= 22 KB; a full year at 10/day ~= 1.6 MB -> negligible, no cap needed. CONCLUSION: fix is two-part (single-connection multiplex + abandon the keyless metered trade-sub in favor of the FREE Bitquery/RPC path); do NOT spend SOL streaming on a 1-SOL bankroll unless streaming latency is later proven necessary.
